A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCOPE study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, with retained material identifiable across renumbering and extensive formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and error analyses for SCOPE.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds CPMPy and PEA comparisons and an experiment on incomplete solver-construction examples.

M1.justification: The agent workflow, solver functions, refinement procedure, inference process, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v1 already permits refinement against multiple examples; v3 evaluates this capability without specifying a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: TravelPlanner and Natural Plan's Trip Planning and Meeting Planning remain the benchmark coverage. Appendix D adds a limited Trip Planning scenario with solver-construction examples missing flight-connectivity or specific-day constraints, extending evaluation to incomplete exemplars.

E2.justification: v3 adds CPMPy across the GPT comparisons in Table 1 and Figures 3–4. PEA, explicitly excluded in v1 Appendix B.4, becomes an evaluated comparator in v3 Table 4. The cost summary also replaces ToS rows with CPMPy rows, although ToS remains in other comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a GPT-4o protocol comparing construction from each of two modified examples separately and from both jointly. Existing benchmark sample sizes, full-dataset comparisons, metrics, model versions, and temperature settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused robustness study asking whether complementary incomplete examples recover sufficient constraint coverage. Existing component ablations, complexity analyses, error cases, and the worked example are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and curves without disclosed experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3 introduces no new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds CPMPy and PEA results and Table 3's 28.1%, 74.4%, and 87.1% incomplete-example outcomes. The cost table adds Meeting Planning cost/time, updates EvoAgent measurements, and swaps the Gemini model labels associated with existing rows. Retained Table 1 scores are unchanged, but new Table 4 gives GPT-5 SCOPE scores of 93.1/87.1 versus Table 1's 93.9/89.5, without explaining different settings.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1, function interfaces, and metric definitions are retained. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in v3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about reusable solver abstraction, autonomous construction, robustness, and efficiency. The headline GPT-4o TravelPlanner result and efficiency claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies single-example sufficiency by constraint coverage and interprets complementary examples as providing union coverage. Section 5.2 adds an explanation based on estimating parameters instead of reasoning through entire solutions. Limitations explicitly adds unhandled domain drift and the need for detection and solver regeneration.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a CPMPy implementation description and repository pointer. Appendix D documents the model and constraint omissions used in the new experiment. Existing model identifiers, SCOPE code-access information, and substantive prompt and implementation documentation are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Michailidis et al. constraint-modelling reference and repositions PEA from an excluded human-assisted approach to an evaluated comparator. The ToS citation changes from Liu to Katz, but the matching title identifies the same work; several other reference changes are publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. Changes comprise targeted explanatory paragraphs, two new appendix sections, acknowledgements, a corresponding-author note, and reference editing. Some apostrophes and accented characters now render incorrectly.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 1, adds Tables 3–4, reformats diagrams and plots, adds CPMPy to Figures 3–4, and expands the cost table with Meeting Planning cost/time columns. Throughout the lengthy appendices, monospaced listings become widely spaced serif text, substantially changing layout and reducing readability.

improvement.justification: The incomplete-example study provides useful evidence about when single-example construction succeeds, while CPMPy and PEA broaden the empirical comparison. These strengthen the paper despite unchanged central results. The gain is limited by Table 4's unexplained GPT-5 discrepancy, inconsistent Gemini cost labeling, and poorer appendix typography; the revision is not a substantial overall improvement.
